questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India, the Supreme Court held that restrictions on internet access can be imposed only if they are:

options.A: Proportionate and open to judicial review
options.B: Approved by the Prime Minister alone
options.C: Applied uniformly to all States and territories equally

questions.explanation: The Court held that freedom of speech through the internet and the right to trade online are protected under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g).

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018), the Supreme Court read down Section 377 IPC to the extent it criminalised:

options.B: Non-consensual sexual acts of any kind
options.C: Sexual acts with animals in private
options.D: Sexual acts with minors of any sex

questions.explanation: The Court overruled Suresh Kumar Koushal and held that Section 377 stays for non-consensual acts, minors and animals.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Section 497 IPC (adultery) was struck down as unconstitutional in:

options.A: Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017)
options.B: Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018)
options.C: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018)
options.D: Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017)

questions.explanation: The Court held that the provision treated a married woman as her husband's property and violated Articles 14, 15 and 21.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Transgender persons were recognised as a 'third gender' with constitutional protection in:

options.B: Lata Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2006)
options.C: Suresh Kumar Koushal v. Naz Foundation (2013)
options.D: Pramati Educational Trust v. Union of India (2014)

questions.explanation: The NALSA judgment recognised gender identity as part of Articles 14, 15, 16 and 21.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court held that a legislator convicted and sentenced to at least two years' imprisonment is:

options.A: Not disqualified until the Speaker decides
options.B: Disqualified from the date of conviction
options.D: Disqualified only after the appeal is decided

questions.explanation: The Court struck down Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act, which had allowed sitting members to continue pending appeal.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Article 245(2) provides that a law made by Parliament shall not be invalid merely because it has:
questions.explanation: Parliament may thus legislate with extra-territorial operation, subject to a nexus with India.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Under Article 254(1), where a State law on a Concurrent List subject conflicts with a Union law, the:

options.A: State law always prevails in its own territory
options.B: Law enacted earlier in time prevails
options.C: Union law prevails to the extent of repugnancy
options.D: Supreme Court must choose between the two

questions.explanation: Under Article 254(2), a State law reserved for the President's assent may prevail in that State.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Under Article 252, Parliament may legislate on a State subject for two or more States if:

options.A: The Supreme Court so directs it
options.B: The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by special majority
options.D: Those States pass resolutions requesting it

questions.explanation: Such a law applies only to the requesting States, and to others that later adopt it.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Under Article 249, Parliament may legislate on a State List subject in the national interest on a resolution of the Rajya Sabha supported by:

options.A: A simple majority of members present
options.C: Two-thirds of members present and voting

questions.explanation: The resolution remains in force for one year, renewable.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: A new All-India Service can be created under Article 312 if:

options.A: All State Governors unanimously agree to it
options.B: The Supreme Court recommends the service
options.C: The Lok Sabha passes a resolution by a simple majority
options.D: Rajya Sabha resolution by two-thirds majority

questions.explanation: Parliament then creates the service by law.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India, the Supreme Court held that decisions of administrative tribunals are subject to review by:

options.A: Only the President, through an order

questions.explanation: Judicial review by the High Courts and Supreme Court was held to be part of the basic structure.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The Parliament of India consists of:

options.A: The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
options.B: The President and the Lok Sabha only
options.C: The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha only
options.D: The President and the two Houses

questions.explanation: Article 79 provides that the President is a part of Parliament.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The official language of the Union under Article 343 is:
questions.explanation: English may continue for official purposes as provided by law.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The eleven 'incidents of ownership', such as the rights to possess, use and manage, were catalogued by:
questions.explanation: Honoré's analysis is a widely cited treatment of the concept of ownership.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: A 'corporation sole' consists of:

options.A: Two or more partners carrying on a firm
options.B: A group of shareholders of a limited company
options.C: A trust administered by several trustees
options.D: A single office-holder with perpetual succession

questions.explanation: Examples include the Administrator General and some religious offices.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The term 'codification' of law was coined by:
questions.explanation: Bentham advocated a complete, systematic code of laws.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Obiter dicta of a court are:
questions.explanation: Only the ratio decidendi has binding force as precedent.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The 'sources thesis', that the existence of law depends on social facts and not on morality, is associated with:
questions.explanation: Raz is a leading exclusive legal positivist.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Locke identified the natural rights of man as life, liberty and:
questions.explanation: Locke's Second Treatise of Government influenced later constitutional thought.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: In Roman law, the 'jus gentium' was the law:

options.A: Of Roman citizens only, in Rome itself
options.B: Common to all peoples and foreigners
options.C: Of the Roman emperor and his court alone
options.D: Of the Church and clergy alone

questions.explanation: It was administered by the praetor peregrinus between foreigners and between foreigners and citizens.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 68 of the Contract Act, a person who supplies necessaries to one incapable of contracting is entitled to:

options.C: Nothing at all, since the contract is void
options.D: Payment from the guardian in his own person

questions.explanation: The liability is on the property of the minor or person of unsound mind, not on the person himself.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 72 of the Contract Act, money paid by mistake or under coercion must be:
questions.explanation: Section 72 is a quasi-contractual obligation.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 65 of the Contract Act, a person who has received any advantage under an agreement discovered to be void must:

options.A: Restore it or make compensation for it
options.B: Retain it without any liability to anyone
options.C: Pay a penalty to the State
options.D: Transfer it to the court registry

questions.explanation: The section applies when the agreement is found void or becomes void.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: A contract to perform the promise or discharge the liability of a third person in case of his default is a:
questions.explanation: Section 126 defines guarantee, with a surety, a principal debtor and a creditor.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Bailment is the delivery of goods for some purpose, on a contract that they shall:

options.A: Be insured by the Government for loss
options.B: Be returned on accomplishing the purpose
options.C: Become the absolute property of the bailee
options.D: Be sold to a third party at once by the bailee

questions.explanation: Section 148 defines bailment; the bailor is the person delivering, the bailee the person receiving the goods.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 151, a bailee must take of the goods bailed as much care as:

options.B: An ordinarily prudent person takes of his own
options.C: The bailor would take of it in a public place

questions.explanation: The standard is that of a man of ordinary prudence in similar circumstances with his own goods.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: A pledge is the bailment of goods as security for:

options.A: Payment of a debt or performance of a promise
options.B: Hire of a vehicle for a long journey abroad
options.C: Registration of a partnership firm and its deed
options.D: Sale of agricultural goods at a mandi

questions.explanation: Section 172 defines pledge; the bailor is the pawnor, the bailee the pawnee.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: In Read v. J. Lyons & Co., the House of Lords held that the rule in Rylands v. Fletcher requires:

options.A: Natural use of the defendant's land
options.B: Proof of fraud by the defendant himself
options.C: Escape of the thing from the defendant's control
options.D: Intention to harm the plaintiff directly and personally

questions.explanation: Injury to a person inside the defendant's premises, without an escape, was held not to attract strict liability.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: The doctrine of trespass ab initio applies where a person entering under lawful authority:

options.B: Pays rent regularly to the owner
options.D: Leaves before being asked to go

questions.explanation: Six Carpenters' Case (1610): the entry is treated as unlawful from the beginning.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Pasley v. Freeman established the tort of:
questions.explanation: A false statement, made knowingly to induce action, gives rise to an action in deceit.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: In Poonam Verma v. Ashwin Patel, a doctor was held negligent for:

options.A: Closing his clinic earlier than the usual hour
options.C: Refusing a free consultation to the poor
options.D: Treating in a system he was not qualified in

questions.explanation: A homoeopath who prescribed allopathic medicines was held negligent per se.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Palsgraf v. Long Island Railroad Co. established that the duty of care is owed to:
questions.explanation: Cardozo J. held that duty is owed only to those within the zone of foreseeable danger.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: The 'classical trinity' of passing off requires goodwill, misrepresentation and:
questions.explanation: The trinity was stated in Reckitt & Colman v. Borden (the Jif Lemon case).

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: The line 'they also serve who only stand and wait', in the context of common intention, was used in:

options.A: Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab
options.C: Barendra Kumar Ghosh v. King Emperor
options.D: State of Maharashtra v. M.H. George

questions.explanation: A person standing guard can share liability for the criminal act under common intention.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: In R v. Dudley and Stephens, the court held that necessity is:

options.A: No defence to a charge of murder
options.C: A defence reducing murder to theft

questions.explanation: The shipwrecked sailors who killed the cabin boy were convicted of murder.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Under the BNS, sexual intercourse with a woman below what age is rape irrespective of her consent?
questions.explanation: The age of consent is eighteen years under the BNS.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Causing death by negligence (other than rash driving) under Section 106(1) BNS is punishable with imprisonment up to:
questions.explanation: A registered medical practitioner acting in a medical procedure is liable to up to two years.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: The distinction between common intention and common object is that common object requires:

options.A: A pre-arranged plan between two or more persons
options.B: A single offender acting entirely alone
options.C: A criminal conspiracy recorded in writing
options.D: An unlawful assembly of five or more persons

questions.explanation: Common intention needs a prior meeting of minds; common object can arise on the spot.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Under the BNS, a Judge acting judicially in good faith is protected even if he:

options.A: Acts out of personal malice against a party
options.B: Acts without any authority at all
options.C: Takes a bribe for the order
options.D: Acts under a mistake as to his jurisdiction

questions.explanation: The protection requires good faith and a belief that he is acting within his powers.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: The general exception of compulsion by threats does NOT extend to:
questions.explanation: It also excludes offences against the State punishable with death.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: An act done by accident, without criminal intention or knowledge, in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner is:

options.C: A civil wrong only, not criminal

questions.explanation: Accident is a general exception in criminal law.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Section 47 of the CPC, questions relating to execution of a decree between the parties must be decided by:

options.C: The executing court, not a fresh suit
options.D: The Registrar of the High Court

questions.explanation: The section avoids multiplicity of proceedings.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A foreign judgment is conclusive under Section 13 of the CPC except where it was:

options.B: Based on the merits of the case
options.C: Given by a court of competent jurisdiction

questions.explanation: Other exceptions include want of jurisdiction, violation of natural justice and breach of Indian law.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Order XXIII Rule 1 of the CPC, a plaintiff may withdraw a suit with liberty to file afresh if it fails because of:
questions.explanation: The court must be satisfied that the suit must fail by reason of a formal defect or that there are sufficient grounds.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Section 24 of the CPC, suits may be transferred between courts by the:
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court has separate powers of transfer under Section 25.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Order XVIII Rule 4 of the CPC, examination-in-chief of a witness is recorded by:
questions.explanation: Cross-examination and re-examination are still done in court.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Order XIV of the CPC, issues are framed from:

options.A: The prayer of the plaint only
options.B: Affidavits of the witnesses filed with the plaint
options.C: Propositions affirmed by one, denied by other

questions.explanation: Issues are of fact or law; they define the controversy to be tried.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Section 34 of the CPC, interest on the principal sum adjudged may be awarded:

options.B: Only when the contract so provides
options.C: Only after the decree is finally passed
options.D: From the suit date to the decree date

questions.explanation: The rate is discretionary, subject to a cap for commercial transactions.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Order XXII of the CPC, if the sole plaintiff dies and no legal representative is brought on record in time, the suit:
questions.explanation: Abatement can be set aside for sufficient cause shown.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 91 of the Evidence Act, where the terms of a contract are reduced to writing, they must be proved by:

options.B: The opinion of an expert alone

questions.explanation: Section 91 bars oral evidence to prove the terms of a written document.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 105 of the Evidence Act, the burden of proving that the case falls within a general exception lies on:
questions.explanation: The court shall presume absence of circumstances bringing the case within an exception.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 24 of the Evidence Act, a confession caused by inducement, threat or promise from a person in authority is:
questions.explanation: The inducement must relate to the charge and give grounds to the accused to believe he would gain an advantage.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 114 of the Evidence Act, the court may presume the existence of a fact likely to have happened, having regard to:

options.B: The common course of natural events
options.C: Past decisions of the same judge

questions.explanation: Section 114 also covers human conduct and public and private business.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Under the Outer Space Treaty, 1967, outer space and celestial bodies are:

options.A: Open to private sale by any State
options.B: Owned by the first State to reach them

questions.explanation: The Treaty treats space as the province of all mankind.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The Chicago Convention, 1944 established the:
questions.explanation: ICAO is a specialised agency of the UN, headquartered in Montreal.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The principle that no State may use its territory to cause injury to another State was affirmed in the:
questions.explanation: The Trail Smelter award (1941) is the classic authority on transboundary environmental harm.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly in:
questions.explanation: It entered into force in 1976; India acceded in 1979.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The principle of distinction in international humanitarian law requires parties to a conflict to distinguish between:
questions.explanation: Attacks may be directed only at military objectives.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Under UNCLOS, a coastal State's continental shelf may extend, where conditions permit, up to:
questions.explanation: Beyond 200 nautical miles, the limit is 350 nm or 100 nm from the 2,500-metre isobath.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Under the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, in appointing a guardian, the paramount consideration is:
questions.explanation: The welfare principle overrides personal law preferences.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: In Shabnam Hashmi v. Union of India, the Supreme Court held that the adoption provisions of the Juvenile Justice Act are:

options.A: Confined to Hindus under the HAMA
options.C: Available to all irrespective of religion

questions.explanation: The Court described the law as an enabling provision for all persons wishing to adopt.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986 was enacted after the decision in:

options.A: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum
options.C: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
options.D: Danial Latifi v. Union of India

questions.explanation: The Act was later read down in Danial Latifi to ensure a fair provision for the divorced woman's future.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Under Section 6(a) of the TPA, a mere chance of an heir-apparent succeeding to an estate (spes successionis) is:
questions.explanation: A mere expectancy or chance of inheritance cannot be transferred.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Under Section 10 of the TPA, a condition absolutely restraining the transferee from alienating the property is:
questions.explanation: Partial restraints for a limited time or to a specific class may be valid.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Under Section 14 of the TPA, a transfer cannot vest an interest later than the life of persons living at transfer, plus:

options.A: Ten years after the last death
options.B: The minority of the ultimate beneficiary
options.C: The lifetime of the next heir

questions.explanation: This is the rule against perpetuities.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Free legal aid for the poor is provided as a Directive Principle under:
questions.explanation: Article 39A was inserted by the 42nd Amendment; the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 gives effect to it.

questions.subject: Legal System
questions.question: The Law Commission of India is:

options.B: A statutory body under the Advocates Act

questions.explanation: It is constituted by Government resolution for a fixed term to recommend law reforms.

questions.subject: Legal Profession
questions.question: Under Section 35 of the Advocates Act, 1961, a complaint of professional misconduct against an advocate is first dealt with by:

options.A: The High Court directly, as a first complaint
options.B: The Bar Council of India directly
options.C: The district magistrate of the area
options.D: A State Bar Council disciplinary committee

questions.explanation: An appeal lies to the Bar Council of India and then to the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Commercial Law
questions.question: Under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015, before instituting a commercial suit without urgent relief, the plaintiff must exhaust:
questions.explanation: Patil Automation v. Rakheja Engineers (2022) held Section 12A to be mandatory.

questions.subject: Dispute Resolution
questions.question: Under the Mediation Act, 2023, a registered mediated settlement agreement is enforceable:

options.B: Like a decree of a court

questions.explanation: The Act also provides for pre-litigation mediation and community mediation.

questions.subject: Education Law
questions.question: Under the RTE Act, 2009, private unaided schools must reserve what proportion of entry-level seats for disadvantaged children?

options.A: Fifty per cent of the seats
options.B: Fifteen per cent of the seats
options.C: Ten per cent of the seats

questions.explanation: Section 12(1)(c) was upheld in Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India.

questions.subject: Gender & Law
questions.question: Under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, identity is recognised through:

options.A: A certificate of identity issued by the District Magistrate
options.B: An order of the Lok Adalat
options.C: A declaration by the Gram Sabha
options.D: A decree of the High Court

questions.explanation: A revised certificate may be issued after surgery to change gender.

questions.subject: Human Rights Law
questions.question: The Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission is a:

options.C: Former Chief Justice or Supreme Court Judge

questions.explanation: The 2019 amendment allows any former Judge of the Supreme Court to be appointed.

questions.subject: Education Law
questions.question: The Right to Education Act, 2009 applies to children aged:
questions.explanation: The Act gives effect to Article 21A.

questions.subject: Right to Information
questions.question: Section 4 of the RTI Act obliges public authorities to:
questions.explanation: Suo motu disclosure reduces the need for individual requests.
